findings.evidence: `Matrix.vecCons` is `Fin.cons` (Mathlib/Data/Fin/VecNotation.lean:61-62); Mathlib has only `Fin.cons_update` (Mathlib/Data/Fin/Tuple/Basic.lean:144), no `Matrix` version — grep for `cons_update` in ./upstream/mathlib returns those two hits only.
findings.fix: State one lemma `Matrix.vecCons_update (x : α) (p : Fin n → α) (i : Fin n) (y : α) : Matrix.vecCons x (Function.update p i y) = Function.update (Matrix.vecCons x p) i.succ y := Fin.cons_update ..` and use it in the four `simp only` calls in place of `Matrix.vecCons, Fin.cons_update`; simp will apply it through both `vecCons` layers.
findings.issue: Four proofs (`bilinMap_update_smul` l.94, `bilinMap_update_add` l.106, `bilinMap_update_neg` l.158, `bilinMap_update_sub` l.178) each delta-unfold `Matrix.vecCons` inside `simp only` so that `Fin.cons_update` fires, each carrying a copy of the same explanatory comment. The missing reusable fact is stated nowhere and the notation layer is broken open in four places.

findings.evidence: Identical three-line `have h : ∀ x, ![a, x] = Function.update ![a, b] 1 x := fun x => by ext i; fin_cases i <;> simp` blocks at lines 113-115, 123-125, 185-187, with the single-instance variant at 165-167.
findings.fix: Extract one lemma, e.g. `private theorem vecCons_pair_eq_update (a b x : M) : ![a, x] = Function.update ![a, b] 1 x := by ext i; fin_cases i <;> simp`, and have each of the four `_pair_*_snd` proofs `rw` with it once (or `simp only [vecCons_pair_eq_update (b := b), bilinMap_update_*]`).
findings.issue: The auxiliary fact `![a, x] = Function.update ![a, b] 1 x` is re-proved inline four times — `bilinMap_pair_smul_snd` (l.113-115), `bilinMap_pair_add_snd` (l.123-125), `bilinMap_pair_neg_snd` (l.165-167), `bilinMap_pair_sub_snd` (l.185-187) — each followed by an opaque `rwa [← h, ← h, ← h]` that undoes the update by backwards rewriting.

summary: Proofs are mostly short and robust, but BilinMap.lean repeats the same two workarounds four times each instead of factoring them into the reusable lemmas they are: a `Matrix.vecCons`-level `Fin.cons_update` bridge, and an `![a, x] = Function.update ![a, b] 1 x` conversion.
